Input Data Layout:
Each item in the input data represents a targeted component accompanied by its full kinematic chain sequence, ordered sequentially from the robot's primary root link (index 0) down to the functional leaf link (last index).

Definition:
The Attachment Root is the host link on the main structural morphology of the robot to which the entire end_effector component assembly attaches. 

Strict Rules for Selection:
1. It MUST be a link belonging to the main body/structure of the robot that remains after removing the end_effector.
2. It CANNOT be any link internal to the end_effector assembly itself (including its own mounting plate, housing, or leaf links).
3. Think of it as the "parent node" in the URDF tree where you would unbolt or detach the entire end_effector module from the robot.

1. Flange Boundary Rule: Select the terminal link of the manipulator arm as the external attachment root.
2. Adapter Inclusion: Any tool adapter, base plate, or gripper housing must be grouped INSIDE the end-effector component.
3. The "Unscrew" Test: If you physically unbolted or detached this entire functional end_effector assembly (including its brackets and housings) from the robot, which structural link remains intact on the main body? That link is your Attachment Root.
4. The Assembly Housing Exclusion: The Attachment Root MUST NOT be an internal sub-frame that is functionally part of the component assembly itself, or the last link before the core robot structure still belonging to that end_effector component. 
5. Traversal Direction & Chassis Edge-Case: Do not fall into lexical naming traps. Trace leftward (towards index 0) until you exit the component's internal tree.
6. Primary Root Fallback: If the component is mounted directly to the robot's primary root (index 0), then index 0 itself is the Attachment Root.

[["parent_link", "joint_name", "joint_type", "child_link"], ...].

Task: Identify the single "Attachment Root" link for the end_effector components provided in the input data.

Each item in the input data represents a targeted component accompanied by its full kinematic chain sequence, ordered sequentially from the robot's primary root link (index 0) down to the functional leaf link (last index).

Definition:
The Attachment Root is the host link on the main structural morphology of the robot to which the entire end_effector component assembly attaches. 

Strict Rules for Selection:
1. It MUST be a link belonging to the main body/structure of the robot that remains after removing the end_effector.
2. It CANNOT be any link internal to the end_effector assembly itself (including its own mounting plate, housing, or leaf links).

6. Primary Root Fallback: If the component is mounted directly to the robot's primary root (index 0), then index 0 itself is the Attachment Root.

[["parent_link", "joint_name", "joint_type", "child_link"], ...].
